Review: halfway

Almost every method so far is the same update with a different target: move an estimate a step towards something better. The methods differ only in what that target is. This page puts three of them side by side on one problem, then maps the first 49 lessons.

The maths

Lesson 6 introduced the shape that every method since has used:

$$\text{New} \leftarrow \text{Old} + \alpha\,\big[\text{Target} - \text{Old}\big]$$

The step size $\alpha$ sets how far to move. The target is the method's best guess at the right answer, and it is all that changes from method to method:

$$\begin{aligned} \text{Bandit (L7):}\quad & Q(A_t) \leftarrow Q(A_t) + \alpha\,[\,R_t - Q(A_t)\,] \\ \text{MC (L35):}\quad & V(S_t) \leftarrow V(S_t) + \alpha\,[\,G_t - V(S_t)\,] \\ \text{TD(0) (L45):}\quad & V(S_t) \leftarrow V(S_t) + \alpha\,[\,R_{t+1} + \gamma V(S_{t+1}) - V(S_t)\,] \\ \text{DP (L30):}\quad & V(s) \leftarrow \textstyle\sum_a \pi(a \mid s) \sum_{s', r} p(s', r \mid s, a)\,[\,r + \gamma V(s')\,] \end{aligned}$$

DP is the case $\alpha = 1$: it replaces the old value with the target outright, because its target is an exact expectation rather than a noisy sample.

Why these targets are sensible: by definition and by the Bellman equation (Lesson 26),

$$v_\pi(s) = \mathbb{E}_\pi[\,G_t \mid S_t = s\,] = \mathbb{E}_\pi[\,R_{t+1} + \gamma\, v_\pi(S_{t+1}) \mid S_t = s\,]$$

The Monte Carlo target $G_t$ has the right mean, but it adds up every random step to the end of the episode, so it is noisy. The TD target replaces everything after one step with the current guess $V(S_{t+1})$: less noise, but biased while $V$ is wrong. DP takes the expectation over $s'$ and $r$ exactly, so it has no sampling noise, but it needs the model $p(s', r \mid s, a)$.

Two questions sort every method so far. Does the target bootstrap (use a current estimate)? TD and DP do, Monte Carlo does not. Does it sample one next state, or average over all of them? MC and TD sample, DP averages. The rest of the course adds a third question: what to do when the table of values is too big to store.
